# Uinta Ice Co.

> Uinta Ice Co. is a residential ice machine cleaning service based in Lehi, Utah. We descale, deep clean, and sanitize undercounter and built-in residential ice machines in customers' homes across Utah County and Salt Lake County, within a 75-mile radius. We have served Utah homeowners since 2022 and we are licensed and insured. Flat-rate service, about an hour per visit, all supplies included. We do not do appliance repair.

We service Scotsman, Sub-Zero, U-Line, KitchenAid, GE Profile, and GE Monogram machines producing nugget, pebble, gourmet, clear, and crescent ice, along with most other residential makes. Our standard service interval is every six months, which reflects the hardness of Utah water relative to the three-to-six-month range manufacturers typically recommend.

## Pages

- [Ice machine cleaning in Utah homes](https://uintaice.com/): what the service is, what builds up inside a residential ice machine (mineral scale and biofilm), why Utah water is unusually hard on ice machines, what a visit includes, and the objection-handling FAQ.
- [Residential ice machine cleaning service](https://uintaice.com/ice-machine-cleaning): the visit in full detail, why the descaler has to be nickel-safe, what to do before we arrive, the end-of-visit walkthrough, how often a machine needs service, and what we do not do.
- [Ice machine symptoms and what they mean](https://uintaice.com/troubleshooting): black slime and mold, low or stopped ice production, bad-tasting or bad-smelling ice, cloudy or hollow or misshapen ice, a clean light that will not reset, how often to clean, what happens if you never clean, descaling versus sanitizing, and what a homeowner can safely do themselves.
- [The brands we service](https://uintaice.com/brands): Scotsman, Sub-Zero, U-Line, KitchenAid, GE Profile and GE Monogram, with the brand-specific quirks, clean-indicator behavior, and common failure points for each.
- [Service areas](https://uintaice.com/service-areas): the cities we serve across Utah County, Salt Lake County, and the Park City and Heber corridor, with local water-hardness figures where a water provider publishes them.
